outlook: Wheat held most of its gains into Tuesday's close, with Minneapolis December spring wheat up about 9 cents near $6.40 and Chicago December wheat up about 8 cents near $5.95, as Black Sea shipping disruptions around the Kerch Strait added risk premium after a stretch of oversold trade. December corn gave back its early gains and closed about 2 cents lower near $4.47 despite a flash sale of 130,000 tonnes to Colombia, and January soybeans slipped about 3.5 cents to near $12.26. ICE January canola rose nearly C$10 to about C$782 per tonne. Traders are still watching U.S.–China trade tensions over new chip curbs ahead of this week's Trump–Xi meeting, a firm U.S. dollar, and Monday's record October NOPA soybean crush of 234.2 million bushels.
